title: Your teaching. In your words.
label: Teacher bio
description: Shape a recognizable teacher bio from the way you actually teach. Keep the training honest, the voice human, and every version consistent.
input: Your teaching language, background, training, and intended audience
output: A schedule blurb, website profile, retreat introduction, or social bio
example: Write my yoga teacher bio in three lengths: a short studio blurb, a website introduction, and a full bio. Ask me for the background you need. Keep my voice and never invent credentials.
note: Includes a facts-ledger method, credential checks, voice questions, and guidance for five publishing contexts.
depth: Completed training vs. work in progress
Voice drawn from real cueing choices

title: Keep the architecture of a class.
label: Class reconstruction
description: Move from messy recall to a clear flow, or a complete teaching dossier. Preserve the side changes, repetition, pauses, and choices that made the class work.
input: Class notes, a transcript, notebook photos, or what you remember
output: A concise flow map, with a fuller teaching dossier on request
example: Help me reconstruct this yoga class as a concise arrow-flow map. Separate what is strongly supported from what is uncertain, and ask about gaps instead of filling them in as facts. Here are my notes: [paste notes or attach photos].
note: Includes movement grammar, source and inference rules, style-specific reconstruction, and a 19-part dossier template with a real teaching script.
depth: Timing that adds up to actual practice
sampleTitle: A flow you can read at a glance

title: Turn reflection into better teaching.
label: Class feedback
description: Make sense of voice notes, class plans, and student reviews. Name what landed, understand what needs attention, and choose a concrete experiment for next class.
input: Your class plan, a voice-note transcript, or pasted public reviews
output: Student practice notes, a teacher self-review, or a reviews digest
example: Help me write an honest self-review of the class I taught. Identify what worked, what felt unclear, and one practical change for next time. Here is my class plan and post-class reflection: [paste notes].
note: Three modes: student notes, private self-review, and reviews digest. Includes templates, a review parser, and evidence-aware interpretation.
depth: A specific moment, not a vague critique
sampleTitle: A useful reflection has a next step
sample: Notice / the second side felt rushed
Return / compare after the next class

title: See the practice behind the numbers.
label: Yoga journey
description: Reconcile years of classes, teachers, and training across booking platforms and scattered records. Keep what happened distinct from what was booked.
input: Booking history, studio exports, calendars, notebooks, or personal recall
output: A reconciled private ledger and a clear view of your practice
example: Help me start a yoga practice log using a manual list first. Keep uncertain attendance visible and separate teacher training from workshops and regular practice. Explain any setup before running scripts or connecting accounts.
note: Momence, Mindbody, Arketa, Walla and more. The method works with exports and available connections; it does not assume every provider has an installed integration.
depth: Momence + a broad source field guide
Multiple classes vs. distinct practice days
sample: Two classes in one day → two visits

title: A little more depth in the morning.
label: Sutra & mantra
description: Let a verified sutra meet the texture of an actual day. A thoughtful reading, a lived image, and an original mantra, with enough continuity to become a practice.
input: Nothing required; share personal context only if you want to
output: One sutra, a reflection, a mantra, and a closing invitation
example: Write a morning sutra contemplation and a short mantra for today. Use only context I have actually shared; if you know little about me, keep it simple rather than inventing personal details.
note: Includes contemplative craft, local-day and duplicate checks, the last 20 verse exclusions, persistent history, and variation in imagery and form.
depth: Verse-led reflection, not a recycled briefing
sample: A line to try, not a state to achieve.
